instructions: address the reader directly as 'you' at least twice
use no sentence longer than twenty words
end every paragraph with a short punchy sentence
text:
Schools must continue teaching handwriting skills today. Many people claim typing is enough for modern life. This view ignores how your brain develops through writing. Handwriting creates unique neural pathways that typing does not. You cannot build these connections fast enough on screens alone. The tactile experience matters deeply for young learners right now. Your memory improves significantly when you write by hand carefully. Studies show handwritten notes are recalled better than digital ones always. Schools have a duty to protect this vital ability from fading away completely.

Some argue that keyboards save time and boost efficiency greatly. Speed is not the only goal of education systems globally though. Clarity in communication often gets lost with quick typing habits today. Handwriting forces you to slow down and think before you speak. This pause allows for deeper processing of complex ideas immediately. Fast fingers on a keyboard do not guarantee deep understanding ever. Your focus suffers when distracted by endless digital notifications constantly. A pen encourages sustained attention that screens simply cannot provide effectively. The physical act helps organize thoughts in logical sequences naturally.

Critics also point to the lack of space needed for writing desks properly. This concern overlooks how adaptable classrooms can become with smart planning easily. Students need dedicated time to practice legible letter formation daily still. Digital tools are powerful but they replace fundamental skills dangerously well if unchecked. You might lose the ability to sign documents without help later on life too. Your personal signature carries legal weight that a cursor cannot mimic ever. Schools must preserve this tradition against overwhelming pressure from technology companies always.

The argument for dropping handwriting instruction is simply wrong and dangerous really. It treats education like an assembly line where speed wins every single time. This mindset fails to prepare children for human connection needs deeply too. Handwriting builds fine motor skills that typing machines cannot replicate ever fully. Your child's hand strength benefits from the resistance of paper fibers directly now. Without this practice, future generations may struggle with tasks requiring manual dexterity sadly soon. We must protect these ancient methods before they vanish forever entirely today.

You should support keeping handwriting classes in every school curriculum immediately. The digital world is changing rapidly but basic skills remain essential always more. Do not let convenience erase the beauty of written expression from our culture now too much longer wait.
